findings.title: Cyberattaque Maileva : six jours de coupure apres une tentative de detournement de la plateforme
findings.summary_md: Solutions numeriques reported on 30 September 2026 that Maileva, the Docaposte subsidiary of La Poste, had been offline from 23 September at 07:00 until 29 September after what Docaposte described as unauthorized access attempts aimed at sending illegitimate mail. The incident was first revealed on 24 September by Cyberattaque.org and FrenchBreaches, who obtained the message Maileva sent to its clients. Docaposte told the outlet it did not yet know whether fraudulent letters had actually been sent.

findings.title: Violations de donnees Maileva-Kiwicare - Hopital Foch
findings.summary_md: Hopital Foch notified patients on 6 November 2026 that payment reminder letters it sends through Kiwee and prints via Maileva may have been read by an attacker who entered Maileva's systems in September 2026. The hospital learned on 28 October that the contents could have been viewed, and the exposed fields cover name, address, invoice number, care date and amount for reminders issued between 9 and 23 September 2026. The notice says Maileva corrected the flaw and that no data was modified or deleted.

findings.title: Flandre Opale Habitat : information incident de securite chez notre prestataire Maileva
findings.summary_md: Flandre Opale Habitat published a notice on 3 November 2026 warning tenants that its provider Maileva had suffered a security incident. The landlord said administrative and financial information such as invoice amounts was taken and that the incident may have allowed unauthorized access to personal data contained in letters sent over the past ten years.

findings.title: Victime d'une cyberattaque, Maileva, une filiale de La Poste, annonce un vol de donnees concernant 22 millions de personnes
findings.summary_md: Le Figaro reported on 14 November 2026 that Maileva, a La Poste subsidiary, had been hit mid-September by a large-scale cyberattack described as one of the largest committed in France, leading to the theft of contact details for 22 million people. The article was among the first national press accounts of the breach.

findings.title: Cyberattaque : Maileva, filiale du groupe La Poste, annonce un vol de donnees touchant 22 millions de personnes
findings.summary_md: Le Monde reported on 14 November 2026 that Maileva, a La Poste subsidiary, had announced the theft of data concerning 22 million people after a mid-September cyberattack. The article noted that a judicial investigation is under way.

findings.title: Data Breach at La Poste Subsidiary Maileva Affects 22 Million People in France
findings.summary_md: Security Affairs reported on 15 November 2026 that a cyberattack on Maileva, a La Poste subsidiary, exposed the names and postal addresses of 22 million people, including patients and tenants. The coverage framed the incident as one of the largest reported data breaches in France.
